## A modular framework for camera-trap reporting

Camera-trap monitoring generates extensive information on sampling effort, species detections, and wildlife communities. Translating these data into meaningful ecological evidence requires systematic quality assessment, appropriate analytical methods, and consistent reporting.

`camtrapReport` brings these elements together in a **modular, reproducible reporting framework** built around the [Camtrap DP standard](https://camtrap-dp.tdwg.org/). It supports researchers, conservation practitioners, and monitoring networks working across sites, datasets, and monitoring periods.

For installation and practical examples, see [Get Started](../index.html).

## Built-in analyses and extensibility

`camtrapReport` provides modules for describing survey design and sampling effort, summarising species detections and capture-based indices, and exploring ecological patterns. Available analyses include species richness, accumulation curves, co-occurrence, activity patterns, habitat associations, spatial detection intensity, and Random Encounter Model (REM) density estimation.

The [**Module Catalog**](module-catalog.html) documents available analyses, requirements, and settings. Report content depends on the selected modules, input data, and methodological assumptions.

Users can select, reorder, and customise existing modules or develop new ones for specific research and monitoring objectives. See [Module Management](modules.html) for guidance on extending the framework.


## Analytical Profiles

Standardised data do not necessarily produce comparable ecological estimates. Differences in filtering, analytical methods, and parameter settings can affect results across sites and monitoring periods.

**Analytical Profiles** support consistent reporting by defining reusable selections and ordering of modules. The underlying analytical methods and parameters remain specified by the modules and report settings.

`camtrapReport` includes default and EOW-oriented profiles, which can be adapted to different monitoring contexts. See the [Analytical Profiles guide](profiles.html) for their configurations, assumptions, and use.
